proof:
Source: steps 3(a) and 3(b) of the parent proof (integrability). They supply the integrability hypothesis of cutoff_calculus for f = 1, (x - y).H and w.

1. Inclusions. If ||x - y|| <= S then ||x - y|| < R. So closedBall y S is contained in ball y R (closedBall_subset_ball), which is contained in closedBall y R (ball_subset_closedBall). Directly, closedBall y S is contained in closedBall y R by closedBall_subset_closedBall, since S <= R. Hence mu(closedBall y S) <= mu(closedBall y R) < infinity.
2. The constant 1. A constant function is integrable on a set of finite measure (integrableOn_const). So 1 is integrable on closedBall y S.
3. The pairing.
 - H is integrable on closedBall y S, by restricting its integrability on the larger set closedBall y R (IntegrableOn.mono_set).
 - The map x -> x - y is continuous, H is a.e.-strongly measurable for mu restricted to closedBall y S, and (u, v) -> <u, v> is continuous. Hence x -> <x - y, H(x)> is a.e.-strongly measurable for mu restricted to closedBall y S (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂ applied to continuous_inner). AEStronglyMeasurable.inner is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch05.Submission, so this route is the one to use.
 - For x in closedBall y S, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives |<x - y, H(x)>| <= ||x - y|| ||H(x)|| <= R ||H(x)||, because ||x - y|| <= S < R.
 - x -> R ||H(x)|| is integrable on closedBall y S. By domination (Integrable.mono', with the a.e. bound for the restricted measure via ae_restrict_iff'), the pairing is integrable on closedBall y S.
4. The weight.
 - closedBall y S is contained in ball y R. So mu restricted to closedBall y S is at most mu restricted to ball y R, and w is a.e.-strongly measurable for the former (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure with Measure.restrict_mono).
 - This restricted measure is finite by step 1.
 - For mu-a.e. x in closedBall y S we have x in ball y R, hence 0 <= w(x) <= 1 and |w(x)| <= 1.
 - So w is dominated a.e. by the integrable constant 1, and it is integrable on closedBall y S.
key_steps: S < R gives closedBall y S within ball y R within closedBall y R, so mu(closedBall y S) < infinity.
Constants are integrable on sets of finite measure.
<x - y, H(x)> is a.e.-strongly measurable and bounded by R |H(x)| on closedBall y S; it is dominated by the integrable R |H|.
w is a.e.-strongly measurable on closedBall y S with |w| <= 1 a.e. there; it is dominated by 1 on a finite measure.
